claims.plain: A classifier trained on foveal V1 during feedback still identifies the same images when they are shown directly at the fovea.
Feedback into foveal V1 carries the shape of the saccade target but not its semantic category.
Frontal eye fields and lateral occipital cortex trend the expected way but fail correction, leaving IPS as the only region that holds.
The saccade target is decoded far less accurately from foveal feedback than from direct stimulation of the fovea by the same image.
Which peripheral target a person is about to look at can be decoded from foveal V1, even though the target vanishes before fixation.
Foveal feedback to early visual cortex carries the target's shape, not its semantic category.
Foveal V1's information about peripheral targets is genuine top-down feedback, not leakage from large peripheral receptive fields.
Foveal feedback during saccade preparation uses the same population code in V1 as an image shown directly at the fovea.
Williams and colleagues found that foveal V1 carries information about peripheral stimuli, which others attribute to receptive-field spillover.
Intraparietal sulcus activity tracks foveal decoding more closely than peripheral decoding, making it a candidate source of the feedback.
When the image is shown directly at the fovea, intraparietal sulcus activity tracks foveal decoding in the opposite direction.
In lateral occipital cortex the pattern reverses: decoding across shape falls while decoding across semantic category holds up.
The analysis linking intraparietal, frontal eye field and lateral occipital activity to foveal decoding was exploratory, not preregistered.
A classifier trained on foveal V1 during feedback should still identify the same images shown directly at the fovea.
Lateral occipital cortex should show the opposite profile to foveal V1, losing shape decoding while keeping category decoding.
Decoding accuracy across early visual cortex should dip at parafoveal eccentricities and rise again at the fovea, not decay steadily.
In foveal V1, decoding across semantic category should fall under feedback while decoding across shape should hold up.
The decoding pipeline, regions of interest and statistical tests were all specified in advance in a preregistered plan.
The preregistration reached OSF only after the manuscript was submitted, so its timing rests on website timestamps the authors cite.
The gaze-contingent display kept the peripheral target out of the central fovea on all but a fraction of a percent of saccades.
Decoding accuracy in V1, V2 and V3 dips at parafoveal eccentricities and rises again at the fovea rather than decaying steadily.
In foveal V1 under feedback, decoding across semantic category falls while decoding across shape stays high.
Foveal V2 and V3 show the same shape-sensitive, category-insensitive feedback as V1.
